result:
The path starts with issue creation, but the current implementation **does not actually call the customer’s endpoint**. It queues a delivery and later simulates sending it by signing and logging the payload, then marks it delivered.

1. In the browser, `IssueForm` in [issue-form.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/components/domain/issue/issue-form.tsx) validates against `createIssueSchema` and submits through `useFormAction`. The new-issue page supplies `createIssueAction` as its `onSubmit` handler.

2. `createIssueAction` in [create-issue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts) uses `withAction` to validate again and resolve the actor. It checks permission and project quota, then calls `createIssue` in [issue-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/server/services/issue-service.ts). That service checks organization scope, the project, permission and quota; allocates an issue number; and inserts the issue. After the insert, it awaits `emit("issue.created", ...)` with the organization, actor and timestamp plus the issue ID, project ID, title, assignee and priority.

3. The listeners are installed at server startup: `register` in [instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/instrumentation.ts) calls `registerEventHandlers` in [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/server/services/event-registry.ts), which calls `registerWebhookListeners`. `emit` in [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for subscribers to settle but isolates their errors, so a webhook listener failure does not make issue creation fail.

4. The `issue.created` listener in [webhook-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/server/services/webhook-service.ts) serializes the event payload and calls `enqueueForOrg`. That function calls `listEndpoints` in [webhook-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/server/repositories/webhook-repository.ts), scoped to the event’s organization. It skips disabled endpoints and those whose stored event-type list does not include `issue.created`. For each match, `enqueueDelivery` inserts a pending delivery containing the endpoint, event type and serialized payload, with zero attempts.

5. Delivery runs separately from the issue request. `startScheduler` and `tick` in [scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts) schedule `webhook-delivery` every minute; `drain` and `runHandler` in [queue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) invoke `runWebhookDeliveryJob`. The authenticated cron `POST` in [route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/app/api/cron/webhook-delivery/route.ts) can invoke the same job directly.

6. `runWebhookDeliveryJob` in [webhook-delivery-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/server/jobs/webhook-delivery-job.ts) claims up to 25 pending rows; `claimPendingDeliveries` increments their attempt counts. The job checks that the organization still permits webhooks and that the endpoint exists and is enabled. It then computes a signature, logs an attempt, and calls `markDelivered`. There is no outbound HTTP request or response-status check.

The retry behavior is consequently limited. `backoffMs` calculates exponential delays of one second, two seconds, four seconds and so on, capped at five minutes, but the delivery job only logs that value: it does not schedule a failed HTTP attempt for retry. A row that remains pending, for example after a worker interruption, can be claimed on a later pass; after its claimed attempt count exceeds six, the job marks it failed. Missing or disabled endpoints and organizations no longer allowed webhooks are also marked failed immediately. The separate in-memory job queue retries a **thrown job error** with its own backoff, but that is not an implemented per-delivery HTTP retry.

For authenticity, `createWebhook` in `webhook-service.ts` generates a per-endpoint secret when the endpoint is registered. `signPayload` computes a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 over the exact UTF-8 payload string using that secret. A receiver would recompute it over the raw bytes received and compare the signature securely. However, the current simulated delivery sends neither the body nor a signature header, so there is no actual wire format to verify yet. The test `POST` in [route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/7cb99ee4-973b-4880-afca-24247be8cf6a/src/app/api/webhooks/%5BendpointId%5D/test/route.ts) returns a sample payload and its full signature for checking a receiver’s calculation; it also does not send to the endpoint.
